gaps.what: the job's name is built as a string, f'app.tasks.{name}' (app/models.py:210), and the worker is started outside the code (rq worker microblog-tasks): the link from the queue to app/tasks.py::export_posts holds only because the one caller passes 'export_posts' (app/main/routes.py:225)
app/tasks.py::export_posts (the job) and app/main/routes.py::export_posts (the route GET /export_posts) have the same name and are two functions: the route enqueues the job, it does not call it

the app's own POST /translate (app/main/routes.py:156) and Microsoft's POST .../translate (app/translate.py:14) share method and path: the outgoing call goes to api.cognitive.microsofttranslator.com and must not be joined to the app's route

url_for('main.index') names a function with two rules, / and /index (app/main/routes.py:25-26): which URL Flask builds is decided at run time; the callers here are written with /index, the rule the inner decorator registers first, which was not checked by running
the popover request is built by concatenation, '/user/' + name + '/popup' (app/templates/base.html:131), and /translate is a literal in the script, not url_for

the pagination links take their URL from the variables prev_url and next_url, the login redirect from the request parameter next (app/auth/routes.py:26), and to_collection_dict from an endpoint name passed as an argument (app/models.py:77)
the forms rendered by quick_form have action="" (app/templates/bootstrap_wtf.html:47): each posts to the URL of the route that rendered it, which only the route-to-template link says

before_request, the error handlers, the user loader, the token verifiers and the two SQLAlchemy listeners are called by the framework on an event, never by a call in the project: after_commit runs on every commit and reaches Elasticsearch only for a Post
Flask-Login's redirect of an anonymous request to /auth/login is set by a string (app/__init__.py:24); the routes carry only @login_required
the reset link in the email is an absolute URL (_external=True) opened from the mail client: no file of the project holds that call
the API has no caller in the project: its clients are outside (httpie is in requirements.txt as a tool to try it)
SearchableMixin.reindex (app/models.py:54) and the shell context (microblog.py:9) have no caller: they are used by hand from flask shell

the session cookie's keys (the logged-in user, the flashed messages, the CSRF token of Flask-WTF) are written by Flask-Login, Flask and Flask-WTF, not by the project: the two session stores here are named by what they hold

Bootstrap comes from cdn.jsdelivr.net in base.html and moment.js from a URL that Flask-Moment chooses (moment.include_moment(), app/templates/base.html:95): neither is in a manifest of the browser side

the Dockerfile installs gunicorn, pymysql and cryptography outside requirements.txt, and no file declares the containers or services of Redis, Elasticsearch, the database and the mail server: their addresses come only from the environment
the database engine is not decided by the code: SQLite in app.db by default, whatever DATABASE_URL names otherwise (psycopg2-binary in requirements.txt, pymysql in the Dockerfile)

three ways to start it, each with its own port: Dockerfile and boot.sh (gunicorn on 5000), Procfile (web and worker; the format is Heroku's but no file names the platform), deployment/supervisor with deployment/nginx (gunicorn on localhost:8000 behind HTTPS). The Vagrantfile only defines an Ubuntu machine and nothing joins it to the rest

messages.html has href="#" on both pagination links although the route computes next_url and prev_url (app/main/routes.py:211-214); _post.html is reused for messages, where the Translate link never shows because a Message has no language
POST /api/users has no authentication decorator (app/api/users.py:45), unlike every other API route
the docstring of migrations/versions/d049de007ccf_private_messages.py says it revises 834b1a697901, its down_revision says 2b017edaa91f: the chain follows down_revision

run_and_observe can register a user and log in with no credentials, but post translation needs MS_TRANSLATOR_KEY, search needs a live Elasticsearch, export needs Redis with a running rq worker and an SMTP server, and password reset needs the SMTP server and the mailbox
the tests (tests.py) cover only the User model: no route, template, job or external call is exercised by them
